diagnosis: All 4 rollouts followed an identical pattern: both PF1 and PF2 were revealed by their owners (A2 and A3) and cited in justification_fact_ids in every settlement, yet checks C3, C5, and C6 failed 0/4 every time. C1, C2, C4, and P1 passed 4/4, confirming the core decisions (streaming architecture, 12 partitions, 400-day retention) were correctly derived. The three failing checks are all ENCODING MISMATCH: C3 expects data_region as "eu-central-1" but every settlement encodes it as "EU"; C5 expects a replay-capacity validation commitment, but PF1's reveal text never mentions that replay-capacity validation is required (it only mentions the burst measurement and partition count); C6 expects a data-residency audit commitment, but PF2's reveal text frames the audit requirement around retention, not data residency, so no settlement produces a distinct data-residency audit commitment.

C6.why: The separate privacy confirmation changes the data region to eu-central-1, changes retention to exactly 400 days, and requires a data-residency audit commitment.

C5.why: The shared tests leave both architectures viable; Ravi's measured 18,000-event-per-minute burst changes the choice to streaming, sets the partition count to exactly 12, and requires replay-capacity validation.

C3.why: The separate privacy confirmation changes the data region to eu-central-1, changes retention to exactly 400 days, and requires a data-residency audit commitment.
